primaryChecks.text: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying,

context.text: “Take a census of all the congregation of the children of Israel, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, every male, one by one,

primaryChecks.text: As the LORD commanded Moses, so he counted them in the wilderness of Sinai.

context.text: They assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month; and they declared their ancestry by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, one by one.

The children of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, one by one, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to go out to war:

primaryChecks.text: Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they offered strange fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children. Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest’s office in the presence of Aaron their father.

context.text: These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the priests who were anointed, whom he consecrated to minister in the priest’s office.
The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

primaryChecks.text: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,

context.text: for all the firstborn are mine. On the day that I struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt I made holy to me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and animal. They shall be mine. I am the LORD.”
“Count the children of Levi by their fathers’ houses, by their families. You shall count every male from a month old and upward.”

primaryChecks.text: The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying,

context.text: “Let the children of Israel keep the Passover in its appointed season.

primaryChecks.text: They kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, in the wilderness of Sinai. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did.

context.text: Moses told the children of Israel that they should keep the Passover.
There were certain men who were unclean because of the dead body of a man, so that they could not keep the Passover on that day, and they came before Moses and Aaron on that day.

primaryChecks.text: The children of Israel went forward on their journeys out of the wilderness of Sinai; and the cloud stayed in the wilderness of Paran.

context.text: In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle of the covenant.
They first went forward according to the commandment of the LORD by Moses.

primaryChecks.text: But among these there was not a man of them who were counted by Moses and Aaron the priest, who counted the children of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.

context.text: These are those who were counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
For the LORD had said of them, “They shall surely die in the wilderness.” There was not a man left of them, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.

primaryChecks.text: They traveled from Rephidim, and encamped in the wilderness of Sinai.

context.text: They traveled from Alush, and encamped in Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
They traveled from the wilderness of Sinai, and encamped in Kibroth Hattaavah.

primaryChecks.text: They traveled from the wilderness of Sinai, and encamped in Kibroth Hattaavah.

context.text: They traveled from Rephidim, and encamped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They traveled from Kibroth Hattaavah, and encamped in Hazeroth.
